variant: Cozy Mark IV (Nat Puffer / Co-Z Development; plans now Aircraft Spruce), O/IO-360 180 hp, retractable nose gear only. Measured geometry from CAFE test of N494CZ; designer figures from Aircraft Spruce specs page

area.note: Designer figure. CAFE data block for N494CZ lists 101.4 ft2 and AR 7.26 (neither consistent with 28.1 ft span: 28.1^2/101.4=7.8); CAFE figure probably includes part of the strake/centre section. Treat reference area as unresolved 88-101 ft2

root_chord.note: CAFE data block, N494CZ; outer-wing root at strake junction. Strake chords listed as 93.5 in (root) / 41.5 in (outboard)

sweep_le_deg.note: CAFE data block 'Wing sweep 23 deg' (reference line not stated; LE assumed). The neighbouring incidence/dihedral/taper/washout values (0 in, 0 deg, '+.75/-.25 = 1 deg total', 1.5 deg) are misaligned in the OCR copy and not assigned here

wing.airfoil: Main wing: modified Eppler 1230 (Long-EZ derived) per CAFE ('Modified Eppler from Long-Eze') and UIUC Incomplete Guide to Airfoil Usage (https://m-selig.ae.illinois.edu/ads/aircraft.html, lists Cozy IV: canard Roncz R1145MS, wing Eppler 1230 mod)

tc_root.note: CAFE data block lists a single 'airfoil thickness to chord ratio 15%' without saying root/tip or wing/canard. For reference, unmodified Eppler 1230 coordinates (UIUC coord/e1230.dat) compute to 17.4% max t/c at 29.5% chord (my calc, E)

wing.winglets: yes: upper winglets with outward-only rudders, plus small lower winglets; leading-edge vortilons (CAFE: lower winglets and vortilons needed for stall resistance across CG range). CAFE: winglet span 57 in x 20 in avg chord each (area printed as '228 sq in', which is inconsistent with 57x20=1140 in2 ~7.9 ft2 - OCR/typo; unresolved)

chord.note: CAFE data block, constant chord; elevator total span 54 in, chord 4 in; canard incidence listed 0 deg

canard_or_htail.airfoil: Roncz R1145MS (also written RM1145S / 1145MS); CAFE, UIUC guide, builder log https://www.deford.com/cozy/chap_10.html

tc.note: E: my computation of max t/c from UIUC R1145MS coordinates (18.8% at 35% chord); not a designer figure

vtail.note: Winglet rudders on main-wing tips, outward-deflecting only, can be deployed together as drag. CAFE: winglet avg chord 20 in; rudder avg span 50 in, avg chord 6 in. No fuselage fin.

length.note: Designer overall length; CAFE lists 17 ft

cabin_width.note: CAFE: width at shoulders 39 in, at hips 36.5 in, seat-to-headliner 37 in. Designer page: cabin width/height 42/39 in

fuselage.note: Overall height 7.9 ft (designer and CAFE, static, full fuel) is to winglet tops, not fuselage height. Side-by-side front seats, two small rear seats; side-hinged bubble canopy. Main gear track 6.5 ft, wheelbase 7 ft (CAFE). No external fuselage width/height found.

gear: Fixed main gear (Long-EZ style composite strut, wheel pants), electrically retractable nose gear; aircraft kneels on nose when parked. Tires 500x5 mains / 4.00x4 nose (CAFE). Hard-surface runways only per designer and CAFE.
cooling: Air-cooled; belly NACA scoop, updraft cooling; inlet 50 in2, outlet 100 in2 fixed, no cowl flap (CAFE N494CZ). Peak CHT in full-power 90 kt climb 491 F. Belly landing brake sits ahead of the inlet: builder's manual warns deployment can disrupt airflow to the engine (see safety).

ntsb_total.note: NTSB CAROL query run 2026-10-24: Aircraft Make contains 'COZY' OR Aircraft Model contains 'COZY' (also 'MK IV'/'MARK IV'/'MKIV' model strings checked - no extra Cozies), filtered to Mark IV by model string/narrative. Events 1995-01-01 to 2025-10-28, includes 2 foreign events (Brazil 2019, UK 2025) and 0 incidents. Lower bound: builder-named registrations without 'Cozy' in make/model are missed. All Cozy-family (incl. Cozy III, unspecified 'Cozy', Long-EZ hybrids) = 42 events 1989-2025.

ntsb_fatal.note: 7 fatal accidents, 12 fatalities (Mark IV only, same query). Fatal: MIA95FA053, MIA08LA096, DFW08LA197, ERA12FA021, GAA19WA595 (Brazil), ERA23FA382, WPR24FA073 (4 killed).

fleet_size_for_rate.note: '350 built (2015)' per Wikipedia citing World Directory of Light Aviation 2015-16. CAFE 1998 designer info: 744 plans sold, 35 completed. FAA registry (ReleasableAircraft.zip, downloaded 2026-10-24): 121 current US registrations whose make/model strings explicitly say Cozy Mk IV, plus 58 'Cozy' with no mark stated. Crude record rate: 22 NTSB events / ~350 built.

safety.pattern: RECORD (NTSB probable causes, Mark IV): powerplant/fuel dominates the non-fatal list - fuel starvation/exhaustion or clogged filters (ERA12FA021 fatal starvation; WPR22LA138 filters clogged by deteriorating epoxide tank sealant; CEN11LA367 gascolator gasket), builder/maintenance engine faults (CEN24LA141, WPR21LA071, WPR17LA048 rotary), undetermined power loss (CEN17LA098). CONFIGURATION-SPECIFIC items on record: (a) belly landing brake deployed in flight blocked engine cooling/induction air -> total power loss, twice (CEN09LA051 serious, CEN21LA351 serious; builder's manual warns of this); (b) main-wing stall that would not recover ('locked-in'/deep stall) on two Mark IVs, both traced by NTSB to build deviations - wrong canard incidence, removed vortilons, wrong CG (FTW97LA009, designer called it an unauthorized conversion) and canard incidence/elevator not to plans (WPR10LA208) - matching the owner's-manual warning quoted by CAFE that aft of the aft CG limit the Mk IV 'could become locked in'; (c) pusher-specific foreign-object damage: canopy opened in cruise and debris struck the prop (CEN10LA245, Cozy family); propeller governor/engine-mount work on the rear engine preceded the fatal stall in ERA23FA382; (d) nose-gear-up landings (ERA26LA030; WPR22LA190 gear fuse). Fatal accidents are mostly pilot/ops (low flight near quarry wall, wires on final, night IMC over ocean WPR24FA073, unexplained CFIT into water). No NTSB finding found for rain/contamination on the canard (R1145MS is the rain-tolerant canard). INFERENCE (mine): the configuration's real hazards in the record are build-accuracy sensitivity of stall behaviour (incidence, vortilons, CG ballast for light front-seat pilots - CAFE notes a 150 lb pilot needs 40 lb nose ballast), the landing brake/inlet interaction, and long, hard-surface-only takeoff/landing (CAFE: 'not a short field or rough field aircraft'; touchdown at 78 kt lost only 28 kt in 3,000 ft of roll without braking). Fuel-management events are common to the type but are not clearly a canard trait.

why_died_detail: Not dead as a design: plans are still sold. Aircraft Spruce bought the Cozy III and Mark IV designs from Co-Z Development (Nat Puffer) and has had exclusive marketing rights since 1 Jan 2004; it also bought Brock Manufacturing's Cozy/Long-EZ metal-parts inventory, tooling and drawings after Brock closed 31 Dec 2005. What limits it: plans-built moldless foam/glass (CAFE: 2,300-2,500 h), ~35 flying of 744 plans sold by 1998, hard-surface-only, CG/ballast management, 180 hp/2050 lb limits. A revival would mainly need a kit (molded parts) rather than new aerodynamics.
rights_hints: Design rights: Aircraft Spruce & Specialty (https://www.cozyaircraft.com/czmain.htm ; https://aircraftspruce.ca/catalog/kitspages/cozyprefab.php). The design rests on a Rutan license for Long-EZ technology (CAFE report: 'Rutan agreed to provide Nat's company, Co-Z Development of Mesa, with a license agreement'). Airfoil: Roncz R1145MS canard (John Roncz). Several derivative/clone designs exist (e.g. Aerocanard, which Puffer called 'unauthorized' in FTW97LA009).
